title: Ang 723–727: Tilang's close
hookLine: Guru Tegh Bahadur, Kabir and Namdev
tomorrow: why does shiny bronze leave black on your fingers?

lines: LIKE WATER FROM A CRACKED POT.
cards: Your water bottle has a hairline crack nobody noticed, and now the bottom of your bag is soaked. Not all at once. Drip by drip.

In Tilang, Guru Tegh Bahadur reaches for the same picture. In paraphrase: if you're going to wake up, wake up now, night and day; moment by moment your life slips away, like water from a cracked clay pot.
The crack is there. The water is going. So is it already too late?

teach.b: His answer comes at the end of the same hymn. In paraphrase: why don't you sing God's praises, caught in false greed, forgetting death? Even now, nothing is lost, if you sing God's praise.
Nanak says, that's how you reach the state without fear. Listen to what that does to the pot. The crack is real, the water is leaving, and the Guru doesn't pretend otherwise.
But he won't call it too late either. Then Tilang closes with two more voices.
Kabir, a weaver in tradition, on ang 727, tells his brother: be still, even for a moment, and God is right there, present.
And Namdev: I'm blind, and your Name, Creator, is my walking stick; I'm poor and meek, and your Name is my support.

teach.h: A GURU, A WEAVER, A PRINTER.
teach.b: So the last pages of Tilang hold a Guru, a weaver, and a calico printer in tradition, from different trades and times, set side by side on one page.
Three lives, one closing chord: wake up now, it isn't too late, and the Name is there to lean on.

how: Guru Tegh Bahadur's Tilang hymns, Kabir's and Namdev's among them at the raga's close, are sung in kirtan; Namdev's 'your Name is the walking stick of the blind' is often quoted by Sikhs.

o: where Suhi, the raga of union, opens

games.q: your grandfather says he's too old now to learn the instrument he always wanted to play. what fits Tilang's close?
o: agree gently; some cracks mean the chance is gone.
tell him to wait until life is calmer and there's more time.
even now, nothing is lost: start with what's in the pot.
games.why: Guru Tegh Bahadur names the crack honestly, then says even now nothing is lost. wake up now, not later.

practice: Pour a little water and take one slow sip. Hold it in your mouth a moment before you swallow, cool, and already on its way. Then sit with the breath, which comes and goes the same way, and isn't gone yet.

wordCard.voice: Ang 723. Where Tilang's last pages begin, closing with three voices: Guru Tegh Bahadur, Kabir and Namdev.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: ghat, a clay pot, also the body; phootai ghat jio paanee, like water from a cracked pot (Tilang, Mahala 9).

carryVoice: Three voices, one ending: even now, nothing is lost, and the Name is there to lean on. Fifteen thirty-four, and onward.
